applied_decisions.identity_authorization: Use **ASP.NET Core Identity with local authentication** for the first demonstrable release. Microsoft Entra ID and enterprise SSO are deferred and are not part of the initial release.  **Tenant and User Provisioning:** - Platform Admin creates tenants and provisions the initial Tenant Admin account. - Tenant Admin manages users within their own tenant and assigns permitted roles. - User self-registration is disabled for the initial release. - Demo users and roles may be seeded using a controlled setup process.  **Role-Based Access Control:**  1. **Platform Admin:** Manage tenant provisioning, platform configuration, and operational monitoring. Privileged access to tenant data must be minimized and audited. 2. **Tenant Admin:** Manage users, assign roles, and manage knowledge documents (upload, update, reprocess, and delete) within their own tenant. 3. **Support Manager:** View authorized team tickets, manage ticket assignments and escalations, and access team-level analytics within their tenant. 4. **Support Agent:** View permitted tickets and knowledge, use RAG chat, submit feedback, access permitted conversation history, and generate/edit AI-assisted ticket summaries, classifications, and reply drafts.  **Authorization Rules:** - Enforce tenant isolation and role-based permissions on every relevant backend API and data access path. - Users must never access another tenant's documents, chunks, embeddings, tickets, conversations, or feedback. - Support Agents cannot manage users, assign administrative roles, or delete knowledge documents. - Support Managers can access only authorized team-level data and assignment operations. - Platform Admin privileged operations must be audited and follow least-privilege access. - AI-generated suggestions remain subject to human review. No automatic customer-facing message sending is permitted.  Implement explicit, testable role-resource-action permissions and negative authorization tests for tenant isolation.,
applied_decisions.knowledge_lifecycle: **Upload Size Limits:** - Maximum upload size: 20 MB per file. - Supported formats: PDF, DOCX, and TXT. - Validate file extension, MIME type, actual file content, and file size before processing. - Reject unsupported, corrupted, or oversized files with clear error messages.  **Retention Policy:**  1. **Original Documents:** Retain while the document is active. Delete when the document is deleted. 2. **Document Versions:** Retain previous versions while the parent document is active. Delete all associated versions when the document is deleted. 3. **Extracted Text, Chunks, and Embeddings:** Retain while the associated document is active. Immediately make them unavailable for retrieval when the document is deleted. 4. **Deleted Documents and Derived Data:** Complete physical deletion from primary storage and indexes within 30 days of the deletion request. Search results must stop returning deleted content immediately. 5. **Backups:** Retain backups for a maximum of 30 days. Deleted data may remain in existing backups until their expiry, with deletion records reapplied after restoration. 6. **Application Logs:** Retain for 30 days. Avoid storing document content, passwords, secrets, or unnecessary sensitive information. 7. **Conversations:** Retain for 90 days, then automatically delete. 8. **Evaluation Data and Results:** Retain for 90 days, using synthetic data only.  **Deletion and Security Rules:** - Enforce tenant-scoped deletion and authorization checks. - Deleting a document must invalidate its associated search index entries, chunks, embeddings, and stored versions. - Prevent deleted or outdated document versions from appearing in search results. - Maintain minimal deletion audit metadata without retaining deleted document content. - Implement retention and cleanup as configurable policies rather than hardcoded application behavior. - Use synthetic/fabricated data only for the initial release.  These limits and retention periods are proposed defaults for the first demonstrable release and can be revised through a separately governed requirement update.,
applied_decisions.ai_deployment: **AI Provider and Technology Baseline:**  Use Azure AI model endpoints for the first demonstrable release, consistent with the existing PRD technology baseline. Use Azure AI Search for vector and/or hybrid retrieval.  **Model Selection:** - Select the chat/generation model from the models available in the Azure subscription. - The model must support grounded response generation, ticket summarization, classification, and structured outputs. - Select an embedding model compatible with the chosen Azure AI Search configuration. - Do not finalize exact model identifiers or deployment names until availability, pricing, quotas, and regional compatibility have been verified.  **Embedding Compatibility:** - Configure embedding dimensions explicitly and ensure they match the Azure AI Search vector index dimensions. - Keep model identifiers, deployment configuration, and embedding dimensions versioned and configurable. - Re-embedding and re-indexing must be performed when an incompatible embedding model change is introduced. - Do not mix incompatible embedding models within the same vector index.  **Deployment Region:** - Select an Azure region based on availability of both generation and embedding models, Azure AI Search compatibility, quotas, latency, and cost. - Keep region and deployment settings configurable rather than hardcoded.  **Budget and Availability Constraints:** - Use small synthetic datasets for the initial learning release. - Configure request limits, token/input/output caps, timeouts, and graceful handling of throttling or service failures. - Track approximate AI usage and cost by feature where provider metadata permits. - Configure budget monitoring and alerts where available. - Finalize numeric budget and usage limits after validating actual Azure pricing and subscription quotas.  **Decision Status:** The Azure AI and Azure AI Search technology direction is retained from the PRD. Exact model identifiers, embedding deployment, region, and budget are explicitly deferred to a technical decision gate before implementation. Keep provider-specific integrations behind configurable abstractions to support future model changes.,
applied_decisions.synthetic_tickets: **Synthetic Ticket Population:**  Use a deterministic synthetic seed script to populate the first release with 100 fictional support tickets across 5 fictional tenants and 10 support agents.  - Use fabricated customer names, organizations, and ticket descriptions only. - Ensure repeatable dataset generation for development, testing, and AI evaluation. - Do not use real customer data or external ticketing integrations. - Maintain tenant associations for every ticket and assigned agent.  **Initial Ticket Fields:**  Use the following initial fields: - TicketId - TenantId - CustomerId - Subject - Description - Status - Category - Priority - AssignedTo - CreatedAt  **Initial Ticket Categories:** 1. Account & Access 2. Billing & Payments 3. Technical Issues 4. Product Setup 5. General Support  **Initial Priority Levels:** 1. Critical 2. High 3. Medium 4. Low  **Initial Ticket Statuses:** 1. Open 2. In Progress 3. Pending 4. Resolved 5. Closed  **Initial Support Queues:** 1. Account & Access Queue 2. Billing Queue 3. Technical Support Queue 4. Product Setup Queue 5. General Support Queue  Use category-based default queue recommendations. Queue assignment and escalation remain subject to authorization and human review.  **Configuration and Ownership:**  - Platform Admin owns and configures the initial system-wide categories, priorities, statuses, and queues. - Tenant Admin manages users within their own tenant but cannot modify the global ticket taxonomy in the first release. - Support Manager can manage authorized ticket assignments and escalations. - Support Agent can review and override AI-generated category and priority suggestions but cannot modify the system taxonomy.  **AI and Data Integrity Rules:**  - AI-generated summaries, categories, priorities, sentiment, and urgency must be treated as suggestions. - Support Agents can edit or override AI suggestions. - Persist the final human-approved category and priority, and retain the original AI suggestion where appropriate. - Validate all structured AI outputs before persistence. - Enforce tenant isolation and role-based authorization for all ticket operations.  These are proposed initial defaults for the first demonstrable release and should remain configurable for future expansion.,
applied_decisions.tools_analytics: **First Release Tool Allowlist:**  Include the following tools in the first demonstrable release:  1. **Knowledge Search:** Search approved, tenant-authorized knowledge articles and return source references. Read-only. 2. **Ticket Lookup:** Retrieve authorized ticket details, status, category, priority, and assignment information. Read-only. 3. **Customer Lookup:** Retrieve limited customer information and related authorized ticket history. Read-only. 4. **Ticket Summary:** Generate an AI summary from authorized ticket data without modifying the original ticket. Read-only. 5. **Ticket Classification:** Generate suggested category, priority, sentiment, and urgency without automatically modifying ticket records. Read-only.  **Allowed Analytics Functions:**  1. Ticket counts grouped by status. 2. Ticket counts grouped by category. 3. Ticket counts grouped by priority. 4. Ticket volume trends over predefined time ranges (7 and 30 days). 5. Basic SLA indicators only when the required sample data fields and definitions are available.  All analytics functions must be predefined, allowlisted, read-only, tenant-scoped, and identify their data scope and time range.  **Role-Based Tool Permissions:**  - **Platform Admin:** Authorized platform-level operational access with audited and minimized privileged access. - **Tenant Admin:** Read-only customer/ticket lookup and knowledge search within their own tenant, subject to permissions. - **Support Manager:** Read-only team-level customer/ticket lookup, knowledge search, and authorized team analytics. - **Support Agent:** Read-only lookup of permitted tickets and customers, knowledge search, ticket summarization, and classification for authorized tickets.  Enforce all permissions through backend API authorization and tenant-scoped data access.  **Customer Lookup:** Include in the first release as explicitly specified in the PRD. Return only necessary customer information and authorized related ticket history.  **Internal Notes:** Defer from the first release. Their visibility, storage, access permissions, and separation from customer-facing drafts require further clarification.  **Write Operations and Human Confirmation:**  - Do not expose AI-invoked write tools in the first release. - Ticket assignment, status changes, customer data updates, knowledge deletion, and customer communications must not be performed autonomously by AI tools. - Any future business-data modification tool must require explicit human confirmation, server-side authorization, validation, and audit logging. - No automatic customer-facing message sending is permitted.  **Tool Security and Operational Controls:**  - Use an explicit tool allowlist with typed input and output schemas. - Enforce tenant isolation and role authorization on every invocation. - Apply timeouts, input validation, rate limits, and safe error handling. - Record tool name, actor, tenant, outcome, timestamp, and correlation ID in the audit trail. - Prohibit arbitrary SQL, shell commands, unrestricted network requests, and arbitrary text-to-SQL.  These decisions define the proposed first-release tool and analytics scope. Additional tools and write capabilities require a separately governed decision.,
applied_decisions.evaluation_thresholds: **Initial AI Evaluation Thresholds for the First Demonstrable Release:**  Use the existing evaluation dataset defined in the PRD: - 50 question/source pairs. - 10 no-answer questions. - 10 prompt-injection test cases.  Adopt the following proposed initial evaluation targets:  **1. Retrieval Quality** - Target: Recall@5 >= 80%. - At least 80% of expected relevant source documents should appear within the top 5 retrieved results.  **2. Grounding Quality** - Target: Grounded Answer Rate >= 90%. - Substantive factual claims in generated answers must be supported by retrieved and authorized knowledge. - Unsupported claims must not be presented as facts.  **3. Citation Correctness** - Target: Citation Precision >= 95%. - Citations must reference valid retrieved source documents and relevant content. - Fabricated or unsupported citations are not permitted.  **4. Abstention / No-answer Behavior** - Target: 100% correct abstention on the initial 10 no-answer evaluation cases. - When evidence is missing, conflicting, stale, or insufficient, the assistant must clearly state that it cannot answer from available knowledge. - It must not fabricate answers or citations.  **5. Structured Output Validity** - Target: 100% schema-valid final outputs accepted by the application. - Validate ticket summaries and classifications against documented JSON schemas. - Invalid model outputs must be rejected or safely retried. - Invalid outputs must never corrupt persisted ticket data.  **6. Prompt Injection Resistance** - Target: 100% safe handling of the initial 10 prompt-injection test cases. - Retrieved documents and ticket content must be treated as untrusted data, not system instructions. - No unauthorized tool execution, cross-tenant data disclosure, secret exposure, or policy bypass is permitted.  **7. Cross-Tenant Isolation** - Mandatory acceptance criterion: 100% denial of unauthorized cross-tenant access. - Test direct API requests, knowledge retrieval, search, conversations, tickets, feedback, and relevant tool execution. - Any successful unauthorized cross-tenant access is an automatic release acceptance failure.  **Evaluation and Release Process:**  - Establish an initial baseline using the versioned evaluation dataset. - Record retrieval results, generated answers, citations, latency, model/deployment identifiers, and prompt versions. - Re-run evaluation after material model, prompt, retrieval, or configuration changes. - Compare new results against the approved baseline. - Document failures, limitations, and remediation actions. - Use automated tests for measurable thresholds and human review for qualitative evaluation. - Do not claim production-level accuracy or security assurance based solely on the small initial evaluation dataset.  **Decision Status:**  These percentages are proposed initial acceptance targets for the first demonstrable release, not existing commitments in the PRD. Record them as proposed decision inputs and require human approval before treating them as formal release gates. Cross-tenant access denial remains a mandatory security acceptance criterion.,
applied_decisions.release_scope_limits: # Revised First Release Scope – SupportIQ (30-Day Boundary)  The first demonstrable release must deliver a functional AI-powered customer support portal with a complete administrative console, configurable security and operational controls, and complete core ticket lifecycle management using synthetic data.  Prioritize the following capabilities as mandatory first-release scope.  ## 1. Administrative Management Console  Implement a dedicated administrative console with role-based access.  ### A. Tenant Management - Platform Admin can create, view, update, activate, and deactivate tenants. - Provision the initial Tenant Admin account for each tenant. - Enforce strict tenant isolation.  ### B. User Management - Platform Admin can manage users across tenants and provision Tenant Admin accounts. - Tenant Admin can create, view, edit, activate, and deactivate users within their own tenant. - Tenant Admin can assign or change predefined roles within their tenant. - Support appropriate local authentication and password reset functionality. - Maintain user activity and administrative audit records. - Disable unrestricted self-registration.  ### C. RBAC and Permission Matrix Management - Implement four predefined roles: Platform Admin, Tenant Admin, Support Manager, and Support Agent. - Implement a centralized, explicit, resource/action-based permission matrix. - Platform Admin can manage system-wide role-to-permission mappings. - Tenant Admin can assign predefined roles but cannot grant additional administrative privileges or modify global permission definitions. - Support Manager and Support Agent cannot manage RBAC configuration. - Provide an administrative view of the permission matrix. - Enforce permissions on all relevant backend APIs, not only through UI visibility. - Prevent privilege escalation and unauthorized cross-tenant access. - Audit all role and permission changes.  Allow controlled configuration of permissions for predefined roles. Defer arbitrary custom-role creation and tenant-specific permission overrides.  ## 2. Operational Limits Management  Provide configurable operational settings through the administrative console.  Initial proposed defaults:  - General API rate limit: 60 requests per user per minute. - AI request limit: 10 requests per user per minute. - Concurrent AI requests: 2 per user. - General API timeout: 30 seconds. - AI model timeout: 60 seconds. - Maximum document upload size: 20 MB. - Conversation context: Most recent 10 conversation turns.  Administrative capabilities: - View and update approved operational limits. - Validate configuration changes before applying them. - Apply changes through centralized configuration. - Maintain configuration version history and audit logs. - Platform Admin owns global operational configuration. - Tenant Admin has view-only access to global operational settings.  Model-specific token limits and exact monetary cost budgets will be finalized after model selection, Azure pricing verification, and subscription quota validation.  ## 3. Configurable Retention and Deletion Management  Implement centralized retention and deletion policy management.  Initial proposed retention defaults:  - Original documents and previous versions: While the document remains active. - Extracted text, chunks, and embeddings: While the associated document remains active. - Deleted documents and derived data: Physical purge within 30 days. - Backups: Maximum 30 days. - Application logs: 30 days. - Conversations: 90 days. - Evaluation data and results: 90 days.  Administrative capabilities: - View and configure applicable retention policies. - Validate retention configuration changes. - View document deletion and cleanup status. - Execute authorized cleanup operations. - Maintain deletion and retention audit records without retaining deleted document content. - Platform Admin manages global retention policies. - Tenant Admin can delete authorized documents within their tenant but cannot modify global retention policies.  Deleted knowledge must immediately become unavailable through search and retrieval. Physical purge and backup expiry must follow their respective retention processes.  Retention settings must be configurable, not hardcoded.  ## 4. Complete Core Ticket Management  Include a complete internal ticket management lifecycle in the first release using synthetic demo data.  ### Ticket Management Capabilities - Create new tickets. - View ticket lists and detailed ticket information. - Edit authorized ticket information. - Assign and reassign tickets. - Update ticket status, category, and priority. - Search, filter, sort, and paginate tickets. - Escalate tickets. - Resolve and close tickets. - Reopen tickets through authorized workflow transitions. - Maintain ticket activity history and audit records. - Support tenant-scoped ticket ownership and access.  ### Initial Ticket Statuses - Open - In Progress - Pending - Resolved - Closed  ### Initial Categories - Account & Access - Billing & Payments - Technical Issues - Product Setup - General Support  ### Initial Priorities - Critical - High - Medium - Low  ### Ticket Management Permissions - Platform Admin: Audited administrative and operational access. - Tenant Admin: Authorized tenant-level ticket visibility and administrative oversight. - Support Manager: Team ticket management, assignment, reassignment, escalation, and authorized overrides. - Support Agent: Create tickets, view permitted tickets, update permitted ticket information, change authorized statuses, and request escalations.  Only authorized users can perform ticket assignments and administrative operations. Enforce all permissions at the API level.  ## 5. Synthetic Ticket Dataset  - Use a deterministic seed script to create 100 synthetic tickets. - Include 5 fictional tenants and 10 fictional support agents. - Use fabricated customer names and data only. - Support creating additional synthetic tickets through the application. - Keep the dataset repeatable for development, testing, and AI evaluation. - Do not integrate real external customer or ticketing systems in the first release.  ## 6. AI Ticket Intelligence and Agent Copilot  Include: - AI ticket summarization. - AI category and priority suggestions. - AI sentiment and urgency suggestions. - Knowledge-based troubleshooting recommendations. - AI-generated customer reply drafts. - Editable, copyable, regeneratable, and discardable reply drafts. - Human review and approval of AI suggestions. - Retention of original AI suggestions and final human-approved values where appropriate.  AI-generated suggestions must never automatically change authoritative ticket data without an authorized human action.  Automatic customer-facing email or message sending is excluded.  ## 7. Knowledge Management and RAG Assistant  Include: - PDF, DOCX, and TXT upload with a 20 MB maximum file size. - Document validation and processing. - Text extraction, chunking, embeddings, and Azure AI Search indexing. - Document lifecycle status management. - Update, reprocess, and deletion. - Tenant-authorized knowledge retrieval. - RAG chat with source citations and abstention. - Conversation history and feedback. - Configurable retention and deletion controls.  ## 8. Analytics and Reporting  Include predefined, read-only analytics functions: - Ticket counts by status. - Ticket counts by category. - Ticket counts by priority. - Ticket volume trends for predefined time ranges. - Basic tenant and team-level dashboards according to role permissions.  All analytics must be tenant-scoped and identify data scope and time range.  Defer SLA indicators until SLA definitions, business calendars, time zones, and required ticket fields are established.  ## 9. Audit and Administrative Activity Monitoring  Maintain auditable records for: - User creation, activation, deactivation, and role changes. - Permission matrix changes. - Tenant administration. - Operational configuration changes. - Retention policy changes. - Document deletion and cleanup. - Ticket creation, assignment, reassignment, and status changes. - Tool execution and relevant administrative operations.  Protect audit records from unauthorized modification and avoid storing unnecessary sensitive content.  ## 10. Operational Limits and Cost Controls  Apply the initial proposed API, AI request, concurrency, timeout, upload, and conversation-context limits specified above.  Additionally: - Enforce configurable input/output token limits based on the selected model. - Track approximate AI usage and cost by feature and tenant where provider metadata permits. - Configure Azure budget alerts where available. - Use graceful error handling, retries, and rate-limit handling. - Defer exact monthly cost budgets until Azure pricing and subscription quotas are verified. - Keep operational configurations centralized and auditable.  ## 11. Explicitly Deferred Features  The following remain outside the first demonstrable release:  - Enterprise SSO. - External CRM, production ticketing, email, and messaging integrations. - Automatic customer-facing communications. - Autonomous business-data modifications by AI. - Complex autonomous multi-agent workflows. - Arbitrary text-to-SQL and advanced analytics. - Internal notes and their associated visibility/persistence workflows. - SLA indicators until formally defined. - Arbitrary custom-role creation and tenant-specific permission overrides. - Multi-region disaster recovery. - Compliance certifications. - Billing. - Custom model fine-tuning. - Automated model selection. - Large-scale benchmarking.  ## 12. Modular Implementation and Verification Approach  Do not prescribe a fixed weekly implementation schedule or sequential week-by-week delivery plan during requirement finalization.  Organize the approved first-release scope into small, independently implementable and testable feature modules or vertical slices.  Suggested feature modules:  1. **Identity and Access Management:** Authentication, tenant management, user management, predefined role management, RBAC, and permission matrix. 2. **Administrative Configuration:** Operational limits, retention policies, deletion configuration, and system settings. 3. **Knowledge Management:** Document upload, validation, extraction, chunking, embeddings, indexing, reprocessing, status tracking, and deletion. 4. **Ticket Management:** Ticket creation, listing, details, editing, assignment, reassignment, status transitions, priority/category management, escalation, and activity history. 5. **AI Ticket Intelligence:** Ticket summarization, classification, priority suggestions, sentiment, and urgency suggestions. 6. **AI Customer Assistant:** RAG chat, authorized retrieval, citations, abstention, conversation history, and feedback. 7. **Agent Copilot:** Knowledge recommendations, suggested customer replies, draft editing, and human review. 8. **Analytics and Reporting:** Role- and tenant-scoped dashboards, ticket statistics, trends, and predefined analytics functions. 9. **Audit and Monitoring:** Administrative activity, permission changes, configuration changes, ticket activity, tool execution, application telemetry, and AI usage/cost monitoring. 10. **Evaluation and Quality Assurance:** Unit, integration, API, end-to-end, security, tenant-isolation, prompt-injection, and AI evaluation tests.  For each module or feature slice:  - Define clear functional requirements and acceptance criteria. - Identify dependencies and integration contracts. - Implement small, reviewable changes. - Include relevant unit, API, integration, and security tests. - Verify role-based permissions and tenant isolation wherever applicable. - Maintain documentation and audit requirements. - Ensure completed modules integrate into the overall application without compromising existing functionality.  Implementation order, task breakdown, dependency sequencing, resource allocation, and delivery milestones will be decided separately during implementation planning based on technical dependencies, available capacity, and development progress.  The 30-day boundary remains the target for the demonstrable learning release, not a fixed weekly delivery commitment or a guarantee of production readiness.  Prioritize essential security, administrative capabilities, complete core ticket management, knowledge-to-RAG functionality, AI-assisted workflows, and mandatory acceptance tests. Defer optional features if necessary to preserve these core capabilities.
